title: Why do Individual Investors Disregard Accounting Information? The Roles of Information Awareness and Acquisition Costs?

scopes.description: Complete author-documented Steps 1–6, including the independent size-BTM and size-BTM-momentum return constructions, intraday TAQ volatility, all main Tables 1–6, and Figure 3 manual graphing. Substantive SAS and Stata programs are embedded in seven PDFs rather than supplied as standalone scripts.

requirements.description: Step 1 reads the author-matched Associated Press earnings-article table oldwork.EA_ticker3_hand. At minimum the code selects GVKEY, DATADATE, RDQ, FYEARQTR, PERMNO, sumAP, an_article, AI_cov, AP_cov, post, and pre for the 2012–2015 announcement sample. The prepared table is not packaged. The datasheet's AP NDA and withheld matching/cleaning code describe historical provenance; they do not establish the current route or sharing status of this exact prepared input.

A trading-date calendar is read as sas.trading_dates_final, master.trading_dates_final, and char.trading_dates_final across Steps 1–3. Required keys include orig_date and trading_date, with event offsets such as plus1/plus2/plus40/plus60/plus75 and min1/min5/min11/min41. No producer is supplied. It must cover the event sample and all explicitly constructed pre-event and future windows.

Compustat quarterly fundamentals feed Step 1 and both portfolio branches. The code uses the 2012–2015 event sample and filters quarterly accounting data beginning in 2010/2011; required fields include GVKEY, DATADATE, FYEARQ/FQTR, RDQ, ATQ, PRCCQ, CEQQ, and EPSFXQ. The exact local product and required fields are readable; period coverage remains a future run validation.

routes.expected_period: Quarterly observations needed for the 2012–2015 event sample and the 2010/2011–2015 portfolio formation filters, with stated reporting and return windows.

requirements.description: Compustat Company is joined to Step 1 and both Step 3 branches for company characteristics and SIC/industry classifications. Required fields include GVKEY, SIC, GIND, GGROUP, and GSUBIND. The exact local product and required fields are readable; future validation can check sample coverage.

routes.description: Exact catalog-listed COMP.COMPANY product with a successful bounded read and matching fields; the local data route is verified.
routes.expected_period: Company identifiers and industry classifications for all event firms and the portfolio universe.

requirements.description: Daily CRSP security data are read in Steps 1, 2, 3a, and 3b for returns, volatility/volume, price and adjustment factors. Required columns include PERMNO, DATE, RET, RETX, VOL, PRC, CFACPR, CFACSHR, and SHROUT. The code constructs pre-event windows, event returns, and characteristic-adjusted future returns through trading day +60. The exact local product and required fields are readable; period coverage is a future run validation.

Step 1 uses Zacks company_info to map CUSIP to ZID before joining Zacks quarterly earnings data. Required inputs include CUSIP, ZID, and the current/inactive identifier fields; no compatible file or current access route is established.

Step 1 separately joins Zacks eps_surp on ZID and report month/year for actual EPS, consensus EPS, analyst count, and report date. This is a jointly required product with company_info, not an alternative to it.

Step 2 reads raw.zacks_preann_raw and constructs earnings guidance indicators in the −1 to +2 calendar-day window around the report date. Required fields include ZID, ticker, measure/period type, reference period, announcement date, guidance values and consensus fields. Current product route and coverage are unknown.

Step 2 reads author/WRDS-prepared raw.ibes_guide and constructs matching guidance indicators around the report date. The code expects ticker, measure/period classification, reference period, announcement date, guidance values and consensus fields. Catalogued I/B/E/S DET_GUIDANCE and DET_GUIDANCE_EXT files are discovery candidates, not verified substitutes for this prepared schema.

Step 1 imports WSH_EA_History_2006_2016.xlsx from sheets 2012, 2013, 2014-2, 2015, and 2016 to match earnings-announcement dates. The workbook is not in the package and no current route, entitlement, or schema has been verified.

Step 1 reads raven.matched_earns for Dow full/flash article matches and joins by GVKEY/FYEARQTR; expected fields include GVKEY, FYEARQTR, EDITION, NEWS_TYPE, and RP_STORY_ID. A local RP_EQUITIES_2012 raw file is not this author-matched product and lacks the author join fields; no producer is supplied.

Step 1 reads ww.matched_IO_2001_to_2016 and matches institutional ownership by PERMNO and end-of-quarter date, using observations from RDQ−100 days through RDQ. No compatible local file or current vendor route is established.

Step 1 directly reads taq.trades_2003to2017 to obtain retail, buy, and sell volume measures by PERMNO/date for event-window variables. This is separate from the TAQ millisecond CTM product used in Step 4. No compatible local source or period coverage is verified.

Step 4 reads TAQ CTM trade files for 2011–2015, retaining symbol root/suffix, price, correction code, time, and date. It filters 9:30–16:01, correction 00, and positive prices to calculate 5-minute intraday realized volatility. No exact local route is listed in the frozen catalog.

Step 4's macro reads daily TAQ master files mastm_YYYYMMDD for 2011–2015 to map symbol and CUSIP/date. It writes temp.master but a later block reads taqmast.master; the required source tables and physical handoff are unresolved.

Step 2 reads master.AI_article_data and merges cons_earn_amt by GVKEY/FYEARQTR. This parsed article file has no producer in the supplied PDFs and is not packaged; expected date coverage follows the Step 1 event sample.
Step 2 reads master.intraday_data as prepared intraday activity data and merges all columns by GVKEY/FYEARQTR. No producer, column dictionary, or compatible input route is supplied.

Step 4 reads home.taqid_merge, with at least PERMNO, CUSIP, FYEARQTR, trading_date, trading_date_plus2, trading_date_min41, and trading_date_min11; it joins TAQ volatility over [0,+2] and [−41,−11]. No producer is supplied.
Step 1 exports Step1_final.csv, while Step 2 reads master.Step1_final as a SAS dataset. The release does not document or supply the CSV-to-SAS import, path, or library assignment.

issues.description: The matched AP article table required by Step 1 is absent. The datasheet confirms historical AP NDA terms and withheld matching/cleaning code, but current access to the exact prepared table is unknown; do not infer that the historical restriction alone blocks that prepared input.

The supplied code reads AI_article_data, intraday_data, trading_dates_final, and taqid_merge without supplying their producers or a compatible prepared input. Identifiers.txt is only the GVKEY/DATADATE sample list and cannot replace these datasets.

The supplied workflow does not document the CSV-to-SAS handoff from Step 1, SAS-to-Stata conversion for Step 2/3/4 outputs, or final dataset path/schema. Step 5 saves Regression_data_Final while Step 6 uses sysuse Regression_data_final; the latter is an author output name, not evidence of a Stata example dataset.

SAS library assignments and WSH paths use YOUR_DIR placeholders, and the programs mix local libraries with WRDS RSUBMIT paths. The executable working directory, host visibility, and writable output roots are not established. Preserve separate library meanings and use relative or [redacted-path-1a992106d3ff] paths with the documented host wrappers.

The Step 3 PDFs invoke %ff48, %Winsorize_Truncate, and %dupl without defining them in the seven supplied program PDFs. Step 2 also includes [redacted-path-ca3c3bb28b4e]. Exact helper versions, source locations, and remote access are unresolved.

The substantive SAS/Stata programs are embedded in seven PDFs rather than standalone scripts. Extraction and line-wrap repair need checking against the original pages before any separately authorized run.

Step 3b calculates MOM and its count into target_benchmark4, applies the n<7 rule into target_benchmark5, then immediately replaces target_benchmark5 from target_benchmark3. Later portfolio matching uses a.MOM. The supplied branch therefore loses the constructed MOM before consuming it; the intended correction cannot be inferred safely.

Figure 3 collapses avol_treat and avol_treat_count, but those names have no producer anywhere in the supplied program PDFs. Whether they are present in an unprovided intermediate is unknown. The documented manual Excel graph step also lacks a graph recipe.

The TAQ master macro writes temp.master, while the later TAQ-to-PERMNO section reads taqmast.master. Both librefs use YOUR_DIR placeholders, and the release does not establish whether the paths are the same or how the generated table reaches the consumer.
